initialVerticalEdit:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: text-free portrait book-cover illustration, 1024 x 1536, 2:3.
Input image: edit target and style reference, the previous cover candidate. Keep its restrained warm ivory paper texture, graphite mechanical cutaway, clear blue-green glass and delicate amber imaging light. Redesign the subject's orientation and composition completely. REMOVE the old title and author from the bitmap; real open-source-font typography will be composited later.

Primary request: stand the entire lens-to-sensor imaging assembly UPRIGHT so the optical axis is VERTICAL, exactly parallel to the left and right edges of the page. Incoming light travels from the TOP, DOWNWARD through the cutaway lens and onto the CMOS plane BELOW. No diagonal lean and no horizontal lens. Rebuild the subject in the new perspective rather than simply rotating the old rendered image.

Composition: the current diagonal lens makes a dense horizontal band in the middle and wastes the top and bottom. Fix that by using a TALL, centered vertical assembly occupying approximately y=330 to y=1310 (about 64% of cover height), with a visually strong silhouette about 600 pixels wide. The cylindrical photographic lens stands vertically, with its large circular entrance at the top and its rear exit at the bottom. A longitudinal cutaway on its viewer-facing side reveals a clear vertical sequence of glass lens elements inside a graphite barrel. Use a high-end technical illustration viewed slightly from above and three-quarter in front, but with the cylinder's axis absolutely upright. All the glass elements are stacked on that same vertical optical axis. Below the rear of the lens, leave a small coherent focal-space gap, ending on a THIN HORIZONTAL CMOS sensor plane centered on the same vertical axis; the sensor's flat active surface faces UP toward the lens and is perpendicular to the vertical axis. Make this a believable sensor and mount at the same overall instrument scale, smaller than the outer lens diameter, not a macro pixel brick. A few restrained support details can relate the parts visually.

Lighting and ray path: a fine warm amber bundle enters the circular upper aperture from directly above, stays contained in the imaging assembly, refracts gently through the glass and converges to a small luminous spot on the sensor's upward-facing active plane. No rays sideways, no diagonal incoming beam, no rainbow fan. Everything uses one coherent spatial perspective. Let the lens and sensor fill the portrait format vertically so the composition feels balanced through its whole height.

Typography reserve: top 18% is calm ivory for a single centered title line to be composited later. Bottom 8% similarly calm for a modest author's name. Do NOT retain the huge blank top and bottom of the previous cover. Keep the illustration inside the left/right trim, with breathing room beside it. Fine soft shadowing grounds the sensor at the lower end; no massive floor surface.
Style: refined scientific nonfiction editorial cover, exact crisp cutaway detail, subtle print-like texture, elegant rather than busy. Limited palette of ivory, charcoal, cool glass and a little amber.
Text: absolutely NO letters, words, characters, numbers, captions, logos or watermarks anywhere. No extra diagrams, rings, separate objects, floating pixels, colored bricks, or full camera body. No book mockup. This must read as one VERTICAL lens → light path → sensor assembly.

Do not extend beams into the top title area.
The bottom area below y=1350 should likewise be calm ivory paper for the author's name; no machinery or shadows there.
Keep the lens body and horizontal sensor as one connected tall composition occupying the central 65% of the cover's height. Plenty of optical detail, but no new objects.
